title: Eastern Air Lines 537
summary: On November 1, 1949, Eastern Air Lines Flight 537, a Douglas DC-4 on approach to Washington National Airport, collided in mid-air at 300 ft with a Lockheed P-38 Lightning being test-flown for the Bolivian Air Force, killing all 55 aboard the DC-4. The Civil Aeronautics Board found the P-38 pilot landed without proper clearance and failed to watch for conflicting traffic, while tower controllers also failed to warn Flight 537 of the developing traffic conflict in time.
probable_cause: The CAB found the primary causes were the P-38 pilot's decision to land without proper clearance and his failure to exercise normal vigilance for conflicting traffic; it also found tower controllers failed to notify Flight 537 earlier of the developing traffic situation, though this may not have changed the outcome.

factors.evidence: the P-38 pilot's decision to land without proper clearance
his failure to exercise normal vigilance in looking out for conflicting traffic
the tower controllers failed to exercise due vigilance in not notifying the pilots of Flight 537 earlier as to the critical traffic situation developing
The two aircraft collided in mid-air at an altitude of 300 ft

events.text: The P-38 requested permission to land due to engine trouble and was cleared by the controller to join the left traffic pattern, but instead flew south and entered a long straight-in approach.
The controller called Flight 537 ordering it to turn left onto a shorter final at the same time the P-38 entered its straight-in approach.
The P-38, considerably faster than the DC-4 on final, overtook Flight 537 a half mile southwest of the Runway 3 threshold.
The DC-4 was cut in half by the left propeller of the P-38 just forward of the trailing edge of the wing, killing all 55 aboard.
